name: x<
translation: “X<”表情符号（闭眼“>_<”眼形与“:<”嘴形组合）
source: Danbooru wiki title x< (page 160136) explicitly states [[>_<]] + [[:<]] = X<; wiki >_< (page 7566) defines tightly closed >_< eyes, and wiki :< (page 8170) defines an upside-down-V closed-mouth frown. This combination proves the tag is the composite emoticon, rather than an English word. Sources: https://danbooru.donmai.us/wiki_pages/160136 ; https://danbooru.donmai.us/wiki_pages/7566 ; https://danbooru.donmai.us/wiki_pages/8170

name: zanburg
translation: Zanburg（Sashizume Soutarou 创作的虚构异星种族）
source: Danbooru wiki page 13790 identifies Zanburgs as an alien race devised by Sashizume Soutarou and describes the species; its other_names contains the Japanese spelling, so this row deliberately keeps the original roman name rather than inventing a Chinese transliteration. https://danbooru.donmai.us/wiki_pages/13790

name: get
translation: 图中出现“GET”字样；不可仅因贴子编号为里程碑而使用该标签
source: Danbooru wiki page 20498 says this tag means the text GET (Japanese rendering also mentioned in the wiki) appears in the image and explicitly cautions against using it merely for milestone post numbers. This establishes the on-image text use, not the common English verb. https://danbooru.donmai.us/wiki_pages/20498

name: ragprof
translation: RAGPROF：Pixiv 上画师绘制《仙境传说》角色档案的主题活动
source: Danbooru wiki page 130869 describes RAGPROF as a Pixiv event for drawing Ragnarok Online character profiles, names the starter yuina_(yuina_h), and lists event rule/template assets. source: Danbooru wiki page 191780 explicitly defines chymlaxi as an alien race from the cyberpunk webcomic Xenosexual. The translation records source and kind only; it does not infer a Chinese species name. https://danbooru.donmai.us/wiki_pages/191780

name: shrims
translation: SHRIMS（6 名来自不同经纪体系的 VTuber 构成的组合）
source: Danbooru wiki page 142021 defines Shrims as a cross-affiliation group of six VTubers, says the name comes from the members’ initials, and lists all six members. This supports a group identity note, not a translated group name. https://danbooru.donmai.us/wiki_pages/142021

name: pincet
translation: 镒子（也指《魔法禁书目录》中垣根帝督取得的同名专用装置）
source: Danbooru tag 603933 has 28 posts; current examples include ordinary tweezer imagery tagged tweezers (20/28) and Toaru-related posts tagged dark_matter_(kakine_teitoku) (9/28), supporting two uses rather than a single inferred sense. Musashino Art University glossary says Japanese pinsetto is named from Dutch pincet and English tweezers: https://art-design-glossary.musabi.ac.jp/tweezers/ ; official Toaru Project chronology says Kakine obtains the pinsetto during the Toaru Majutsu no Index arc: https://toaru-project.com/world/chronicle/ . The translation preserves the ordinary meaning and identifies the series-specific device without inventing a full technical name.

name: funbuns
source: Danbooru wiki snapshot has no exact funbuns wiki page. The tag’s four sampled Danbooru posts (4086220, 2837661, 1362215, 1103543) are all Ar tonelico character images. The Ar tonelico item guide lists Funbun as food sold by the Funbun Seller, and the game dialogue guide explicitly labels “The Snack, Funbun” and discusses eating them. Together these verify that this is the franchise’s food/item term, not a generic “fun buns” phrase. https://danbooru.donmai.us/posts/4086220 ; https://danbooru.donmai.us/posts/2837661 ; https://www.neoseeker.com/ar-tonelico/faqs/179355-talk.html ; https://exapico.wiki.gg/wiki/List_of_Usable_Items_in_Ar_tonelico%3A_Melody_of_Elemia

name: archouchou
translation: Archouchou（《Re:Stage!》由 Sorano Neon、Furumi Chie、Futaba Shiho 组成的三人偶像组合）
source: Danbooru wiki page 252511 identifies Archouchou as a fictional idol group in Re:Stage!, says to use the tag only when all three members are prominent, and names Sorano Neon, Furumi Chie, Futaba Shiho. The Re:Stage! unveiling event title and official talent-agency event notice independently use the unit name Archouchou. name: olofboost
translation: Olofboost：《CS:GO》DreamHack Winter 2014 Overpass 地图上利用像素越界点位的助推投机战术
source: Danbooru wiki page 228122 says Olofboost is the tactic used by Fnatic player Olof “olofmeister” Kajbjer against LDLC on Overpass during DreamHack Winter 2014: a pixel-walking boost to reach unintended sightlines, later deemed an exploit. It links the match video. This verifies a named Counter-Strike incident, not a generic boost. https://danbooru.donmai.us/wiki_pages/228122 ; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DqB95s47f1w
